Description: Young, fiercely combative, and possessed of a formidable martial physique, he commands natural authority among the youthful knights of the realm. In 1259, exasperated by the cynical temporizing of his father Richard and the elderly magnates, Gilbert gravitated toward Simon de Montfort's bold, reformist rhetoric, dreaming of sweeping aristocratic renewal. Yet beneath his hot-headed crusading zeal lies the unyielding arrogance of a Marcher warlord who will bend the knee to no master. A natural kingmaker, Gilbert possesses a volatile dynamism that will see him knighted by Montfort and capture King Henry III at Lewes, only to switch sides and spearhead Prince Edward's vengeance at Evesham when Montfort's power becomes unbearable. Driven by fiery pride, he is a force of political devastation waiting to detonate.
Motivations: Break free from the timid caution of elder magnates and forge a reputation in battle
Exact bloody retribution upon Llywelyn's Welsh raiders and plant Clare banners across the hills
Side with Simon de Montfort to purge royal favorites and install martial leadership in London
Values: Glory is won by cold steel on the battlefield; cowardly compromise is a permanent disgrace
Allegiance is pledged only to worthy warlords; when an ally turns tyrant, defection is duty
The fiery blood of Clare kneels to neither king nor council
Fears: Languishing in tedious diplomatic compromises, played as a tool by entrenched elders
Seeing Welsh incursions dismantle his Marcher holdings while royal officials look on
SpeechStyle: Speaks in a loud, rapid, and aggressive cadence, laced with mocking defiance. He scorns timid diplomacy, slamming his gauntlets on the table when challenged by older magnates.
